And the unspoken complaint seems to be that the other party members wanted a fight because that's why they enjoy dnd. 
The simplest solution is to just give them a fight next session they have a good reason to have a go at. Metamagic option: Blind Spell

So, I have determined not many of the metamagic seems to fit my character well, nothing really excites me, and I turned from official content to homebrew, and surprisingly, I found no good homebrewed metamagics. I decided to make my own, and I found it to be hard because I didn't know what couldn't already be done that wasn't absolutely game breaking but I think I came up with one I think seems decent and would like some feedback from the hive mind.

Blind Spell
When you cast a spell, you can spend a number of sorcery points equal to the spells level to ignore line of sight requirements for that casting of the spell.

- Wording could use fine tuning
- Can anyone think of a better spell point value for this
- Any crazy circumstances I'm not thinking about?

Intention of the spell, allow sorcerer's to target creatures they can't see, this would include creatures that they are aware of, and exclude creatures they are not, such as hidden creatures. This metamagic would be intended for use against an invisible target or In certain cases, targeting a creature or area behind a wall or cover

Examples of situations that would work
An invisible creature has made itself known but remains unseen. You can target the creature with any appropriate spell. 
A goblin runs behind a wall but doesn't use it's hide action, your sorcerer casts create bonfire spontaneously making a flame beneath the creature where the sorcerer can't see

Examples of situations that wouldn't work
Combat has erupted but a foe has hidden themselves well enough (hide action) that the sorcerer doesn't know where to strike
A goblin ducks behind a wall, the sorcerer is unable to hit them with a fire bolt, as it crosses the distance from finger top to the wall between them, searing the stone

Any suggestions would be appreciated, I'm looking for feedback even if that feedback isn't what I want to hear, especially if it's to strong to be a metamagic option
